Package com.bilt.pos.platform

Class OkHttpPlatformClient

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.platform.OkHttpPlatformClient
All Implemented Interfaces:
BiltPlatformClient, AutoCloseable
public final class OkHttpPlatformClient extends Object implements BiltPlatformClient
BiltPlatformClient over OkHttp with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication. 

 BiltPlatformClient client = OkHttpPlatformClient.builder()
     .credentials(BiltCredentials.clientCredentials(clientId, clientSecret))
     .environment(BiltEnvironment.STAGING)
     .build();

 PlatformResponse response = client.execute(
     PlatformRequest.post("v1/example").jsonBody("{}").build());

The first request acquires an access token from the environment's token endpoint; later requests reuse it. The token is refreshed on a background thread a little before it expires, so callers do not pay for the token exchange in the normal case. When the platform answers 401 the token is discarded, re-acquired and the request is sent once more; a second 401 is returned to the caller as an ordinary response. Concurrent callers who all need a token share one token request.

Without an explicit OkHttpClient the client creates its own with a 10 s connect and 30 s call timeout, and releases its pool and threads on close(). A supplied client is used as is and left running on close, since its owner may share it. Per-request timeouts bound the exchange with the API and, separately, the wait for a token that the exchange may have to make first.
